_comment: Fund Q&A bank for the Pep multi-fund mode. Source documents in docs/fund-data/. Manually curated — review against PDFs before pitch. Keep answers short (1-3 sentences) since Pep reads them aloud.

answers.fund_overview: The OC Mid-Cap Fund is a benchmark-unaware managed investment scheme investing in a diversified portfolio of listed mid-cap securities on the ASX and NZX. It typically holds 25 to 50 stocks and aims to outperform the S&P/ASX MidCap 50 Accumulation Index by 2% over rolling five-year periods after fees and taxes.
answers.investment_objective: The Fund aims to outperform the S&P/ASX MidCap 50 Accumulation Index by 2% over rolling five-year periods, after fees and taxes. There is no guarantee that this objective will be achieved.
answers.investment_strategy: OC undertakes detailed bottom-up fundamental analysis to identify mid-cap securities trading below their intrinsic value with sound investment fundamentals and the potential for strong long-term returns. The portfolio is overseen by the OC Risk Management Committee and may include a small allocation to shorter-term event-driven or macro thematic positions.
answers.investment_universe: The Fund invests primarily in companies in the S&P/ASX MidCap 50 Index. Up to 20% of the portfolio may be held in S&P/ASX 50 names, and up to 20% in liquid, high-conviction companies outside the S&P/ASX 100. New Zealand listings up to 10% are also permitted.
answers.asset_allocation: Australian listed securities can range from 0 to 100% of the portfolio, cash 0 to 20%, and New Zealand listed securities 0 to 10%. The maximum ownership of any single company is 7.5%. The Fund does not borrow.
answers.investment_timeframe: The recommended investment horizon is five years or more. This is a guide only, not a recommendation.
answers.risk_level: High. The likelihood of your investment going down in the short term is relatively high compared to investments in fixed interest or cash. The Fund is not suitable for short-term investors or those who cannot sustain a loss of investment capital.
answers.target_market: The Fund suits investors seeking diversified exposure to quality Australian mid-cap companies, those complementing direct large-cap holdings or large-cap managed funds, investors looking for an active investment approach, and those with an investment horizon of five years or more.
answers.management_fees: Management fees and costs are 0.85% per annum of the net asset value of the Fund, calculated daily and paid monthly in arrears.
answers.performance_fees: A performance fee of 15.375% is accrued daily on excess performance above the benchmark within a performance period, after deducting the management fee. It only becomes payable when the Fund's return is positive and above the high-water mark. Estimated at 0.53% of NAV.
answers.transaction_costs: Transaction costs are estimated at 0.38% of NAV. The buy/sell spread is plus 0.25% on investments and minus 0.25% on withdrawals, charged into the Fund and reflected in the application and withdrawal unit prices.
answers.minimum_investment: The minimum initial investment is $20,000. Additional investments are a minimum of $5,000 and the minimum withdrawal is $5,000. The minimum account balance is $20,000.
answers.distributions: Net income and realised capital gains are distributed annually, usually within two months following the end of the financial year. Distributions can be paid into a nominated bank account or reinvested as additional units. Distribution amounts vary year to year and are not guaranteed.
answers.withdrawals: You can withdraw all or part of your investment at any time using the Withdrawal Request Form. Requests received and accepted by 2pm AEST on a business day are processed at that day's exit price. Proceeds are usually paid within ten business days.
answers.cooling_off: Retail investors have a 14-day cooling-off period after applying. The amount repaid is adjusted for market movements, reasonable administration and transaction costs, and any relevant taxes or duties — so you may receive back less than you originally invested.
answers.about_oc: OC Funds Mid-Cap Pty Ltd is a boutique investment manager established in 2000 specialising in Australian mid, small and micro-cap equities. The team is led by Robert Frost and comprises six specialist investors with combined experience of over 100 years. Investment team members are owners of the Investment Manager and material investors in the Fund.
answers.about_copia: Copia Investment Partners Ltd is the responsible entity. Its role is to hold the Fund's assets on trust for investors and invest them in accordance with the Fund's constitution and applicable laws. Copia is governed by the Fund's constitution, the Corporations Act and general trust law.
answers.how_to_apply: Direct investors can apply online at OC Mid-Cap Fund Online Application or by submitting a paper form. Indirect investors apply through their platform operator. Applications received by 2pm AEST on a business day are processed at that day's entry price.
answers.tax: The Fund has elected to be an Attribution Managed Investment Trust from the 2024 financial year, so it does not pay tax on behalf of resident investors. Investors include their attributed share of the Fund's net taxable income — disclosed on an AMMA statement issued after year-end — in their assessable income. Investors should consult their own tax adviser.
answers.esg: The responsible entity does not take ESG considerations into account when making investment decisions. The Investment Manager may take ESG factors into account at its discretion where relevant to the financial performance of the investment, but does not have a predetermined view.
answers.performance: Current performance figures are published on the OC Funds website. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future performance.

answers.fund_overview: The OC Micro-Cap Fund is a long-only, benchmark-unaware managed investment scheme that invests in micro-capitalisation companies — defined as those with a market cap under $500 million at the time of initial acquisition — listed or about to list on the ASX or NZX. Targets strong long-term capital growth from sustainable business models.
answers.investment_objective: The Fund aims to provide a total return after fees and expenses of 5% plus the S&P/ASX Emerging Companies Accumulation Index over a rolling five-year period.
answers.investment_strategy: OC's investment universe focuses on companies outside the S&P/ASX 300 Index — often under-researched, which can lead to mispricing opportunities. Detailed bottom-up fundamental analysis identifies securities trading below intrinsic value, complemented by a small allocation to quality concept stocks with robust business models and a path to profitability within five years.
answers.investment_universe: Securities listed or about to list on the ASX or NZX, primarily companies outside the S&P/ASX 300 Index with market caps under $500 million at the time of acquisition. Up to 20% may be held in S&P/ASX 300 names and up to 10% in foreign listed (NZX) securities.
answers.asset_allocation: Australian listed securities range from 70 to 100%, cash 0 to 20%, S&P/ASX 300 listed securities up to 20%, unlisted securities up to 10%, and foreign listed securities up to 10%. Maximum ownership of any company is 7.5%, maximum absolute stock position 8%. The Fund does not buy or write third-party derivatives.
answers.investment_timeframe: The recommended investment horizon is five years or more. This is a guide only, not a recommendation.
answers.risk_level: High. The likelihood of your investment going down in the short term is relatively high compared to funds investing in fixed interest or cash. The Fund is not suitable for short-term investors or those unable to sustain a loss of investment capital.
answers.target_market: Investors seeking strong long-term capital growth from a benchmark-unaware exposure to Australian and New Zealand micro-cap companies, prepared to accept a high level of risk and volatility for at least five years.
answers.management_fees: Management fees and costs are 1.20% per annum of the net asset value of the Fund, calculated daily and paid monthly in arrears.
answers.performance_fees: A performance fee of 20.5% is payable quarterly on any excess performance above the benchmark within a performance period, after deducting the management fee, subject to a high-water mark. Estimated at 0.40% of NAV.
answers.transaction_costs: Transaction costs are estimated at 0.20% of NAV. The buy/sell spread is plus 0.30% on investments and minus 0.30% on withdrawals.
answers.minimum_investment: The minimum initial investment is $5,000. Additional investments, withdrawals and switches all have a minimum of $1,000. The minimum account balance is $5,000.
answers.distributions: Net income and realised capital gains are distributed annually, usually within two months following 30 June. Distributions can be paid into a nominated bank account or reinvested as additional units. Amounts vary year to year and are not guaranteed.
answers.withdrawals: You can withdraw all or part of your investment by completing a Withdrawal Request Form. Requests received by 2pm Melbourne time are processed same day. Proceeds are usually paid within five business days. Withdrawals may be suspended for up to 60 days when in the best interests of investors.
answers.cooling_off: Retail investors have a 14-day cooling-off period. The amount repaid is adjusted for market movements, reasonable administration and transaction costs, and any relevant taxes — so you may receive back less than you originally invested.
answers.about_oc: OC Funds is a boutique investment manager established in 2000 specialising in Australian mid, small and micro-cap equities. The team applies bottom-up fundamental analysis with an emphasis on screening out complex or speculative businesses, and is materially invested in the funds it manages.
answers.about_copia: Copia Investment Partners Ltd is the responsible entity. Its role is to hold the Fund's assets on trust for investors and invest them in accordance with the Fund's constitution and applicable laws.
answers.how_to_apply: Apply by completing the OC Micro-Cap Fund Application Form attached to the PDS, or via online application. Applications received and accepted by 2pm Melbourne time are processed at that day's entry price. Indirect investors apply through their platform operator.
answers.tax: The Fund is a registered managed investment scheme that does not generally pay tax on behalf of resident investors. Investors include their attributed share of the Fund's net taxable income in their assessable income each year. Investors should consult their own tax adviser.
answers.esg: Labour standards and environmental, social and ethical considerations are taken into account when making investment decisions for the Fund.
answers.performance: Current performance figures are published on the OC Funds website. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future performance.

answers.fund_overview: The OC Premium Small Companies Fund is a long-only, benchmark-unaware managed investment scheme investing in Australian small companies, primarily outside the S&P/ASX 100 Index. It typically holds 30 to 50 stocks and aims to outperform the S&P/ASX Small Ordinaries Total Return Index by 3 to 5% per annum over rolling five-year periods before fees and taxes.
answers.investment_objective: To outperform the S&P/ASX Small Ordinaries Total Return Index by 3 to 5% per annum over rolling five-year periods, before fees and taxes.
answers.investment_strategy: OC takes a stock-specific, bottom-up approach with no particular style bias — they don't lean value, growth, or yield. The focus is on smaller businesses outside the ASX 100 in the belief these are easier to understand, simpler to value, and accessible to research. OC favours strong management teams and well-resourced specialists in niche sectors with growth potential.
answers.investment_universe: Securities listed on the ASX outside the S&P/ASX 100 Index. The Fund may invest in S&P/ASX 100 names where consistent with the investment strategy.
answers.asset_allocation: Australian listed securities 80 to 100%, cash 0 to 20%. The number of stocks held is generally between 30 and 50. The portfolio diversification of this Fund is low.
answers.investment_timeframe: The minimum suggested investment timeframe is at least 7 years per the CFS factsheet, with the TMD setting at least 5 years.
answers.risk_level: Very high to high. The Fund is rated as a satellite or small allocation product — typically suitable for up to 25% of an investor's total investable assets — for consumers with a very-high to high risk and return profile.
answers.target_market: Investors seeking capital growth as a satellite allocation within a portfolio, with a minimum investment timeframe of five years, a very-high to high risk and return profile, and a need for daily access to capital.
answers.management_fees: Refer to the latest PDS for current management fees and costs. Fees are deducted from the Fund and reflected in the daily unit price.
answers.performance_fees: Refer to the latest PDS for the current performance fee structure. Performance fees are typically calculated on excess performance above the benchmark, subject to a high-water mark.
answers.transaction_costs: Refer to the latest PDS for current transaction costs and buy/sell spread. The buy/sell spread is reflected in the application and withdrawal unit prices.
answers.minimum_investment: Refer to the latest PDS for current minimum investment, additional investment and withdrawal amounts.
answers.distributions: Net income and realised capital gains are distributed quarterly — distributions are typically paid in February, May, August and November based on historical patterns shown in the CFS factsheet. Amounts vary year to year and are not guaranteed.
answers.withdrawals: You have daily access to your capital. Refer to the latest PDS for the current withdrawal process, cut-off times and payment timeframe.
answers.cooling_off: Retail investors have a 14-day cooling-off period. The amount repaid is adjusted for market movements, reasonable administration and transaction costs, and any relevant taxes — so you may receive back less than you originally invested.
answers.about_oc: OC Funds is a boutique investment manager established in 2000 specialising in Australian mid, small and micro-cap equities. Bottom-up, stock-specific approach with no style bias, focused on companies outside the ASX 100 that are easier to understand and accessible to research.
answers.about_copia: Copia Investment Partners Ltd is the responsible entity. The product is also offered as a Colonial First State FirstChoice investment option, with Avanteos Investments Limited as trustee and CFSIL as responsible entity for that wrapper.
answers.how_to_apply: Apply directly via Copia or through a platform such as Colonial First State FirstChoice. Refer to the relevant PDS and Financial Services Guide before investing.
answers.tax: Investing in a registered managed investment scheme is likely to have tax consequences. Investors include their share of the Fund's distributed income in their assessable income each year. Investors should seek professional tax advice.
answers.esg: Refer to the latest PDS for the Fund's current ESG considerations and any labour standards or environmental, social or ethical factors taken into account in investment decisions.
answers.performance: Per the CFS factsheet dated January 2026: the Fund returned 7.02% per annum over three years and 5.20% per annum over five years (Investments option). Since inception in May 2015, returns are 7.57% per annum, versus the benchmark of 11.28% per annum. Past performance is not an indicator of future performance.
